scope: Resolve A/B feature disagreements only after both independent receipts are frozen, without overwriting either source receipt.
preconditions: both receipts bind the same packet_template_sha256
both receipts bind the same feature_schema_sha256
both receipts bind the same source slice sha256 for the item

may_see: coder A value and evidence pointer
coder B value and evidence pointer
declared philological aids used by each coder
must_not_see: which resolution would strengthen or weaken the research hypothesis

resolution_ladder.rule: If either coder used the wrong slice/version, do not arbitrate the semantic value; issue a procedural correction receipt and recode independently.
Resolve only against the preregistered feature definition; no feature broadening or narrowing after seeing the disagreement.
Explicit locus evidence outranks inference. Lack of explicit support cannot be repaired by narrative plausibility.
For rare_lexical_or_formulaic_correspondence, modern translation wording alone cannot resolve to PRESENT.
If the frozen evidence does not decide the feature, arbitrate to UNKNOWN rather than force PRESENT or ABSENT.

forbidden_resolution_methods: choose the value that improves expected clustering
average coder labels into a pseudo-value
rewrite the feature definition after seeing conflict
use model consensus as textual evidence
preservation_rule: Arbitration creates a third immutable receipt. It never edits or deletes coder A/B receipts.
instability_rule: Agreement statistics are reported descriptively but do not create truth authority. A large disagreement burden may trigger ontology review before scoring, but cannot be hidden by arbitration.
